question: Despite the repeated appeals of the Director of the Cardiology Clinic and the unanimous opinions of the Scientific Council and the Medical Service, the central patient monitoring unit of the Coronary Unit of Kilkis Hospital has remained out of operation for a year.

The equipment, essential for the continuous monitoring of patients with acute coronary syndromes, remains in storage unused, despite the existence of an available system that could be temporarily transferred from the ICU. The unjustified delay in activating this equipment puts human lives at immediate risk and demonstrates serious dysfunctions in the administrative management of the hospital. In view of the above: 1.
How does the Commission assess the failure of the Greek authorities to ensure the basic functioning of a critical medical unit for an entire year?
Does the Commission intend to investigate whether this inaction constitutes a breach of the minimum standards of safety and quality of healthcare provided for in Directive 2011/24/EU?
What actions can the Commission take to ensure the immediate operational adequacy of the Cardiology Clinic of Kilkis Hospital?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.1.2026) As per Article 168(7) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union1, Member States are responsible for the organisation and delivery of health services and medical care, including their management and the allocation of the resources assigned to them.

EU tools and initiatives support Member States to strengthen health systems via knowledge sharing, technical assistance, funding, and policy guidance2. For example, the European Semester provides country-specific recommendations and the State of Health in the EU cycle3 includes country-specific analyses.

Directive 2011/24/EU4 aims to facilitate access to cross-border healthcare within the EU, ensuring patients' rights to seek treatment in Member States other than their own while establishing rules for reimbursement. It seeks to enhance cooperation and information exchange between health systems across the EU.

Member States are competent to establish and implement minimum standards of safety and quality of healthcare services. National authorities are competent to investigate alleged breaches. Greece can use EU funding from the EU4Health programme, the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) or the Cohesion Policy Funds.

Under the RRF, Member States design national recovery and resilience plans outlining reforms and investments addressing country-specific challenges identified in the Semester. Those policy actions shall be in line with EU objectives and meet the specific RRF requirements.
